goals: Route newly acquired matching items into deterministic occupied destinations, including supported unlocked carried shulker boxes and bundles, without changing exact item or component identity.
Preserve established passive-pickup, external QUICK_MOVE, and player-origin QUICK_MOVE behavior across vanilla and Inventory Extended storage while composing safely with Offhand Shift-Click QoL.
Provide a server-authoritative lock control that excludes selected carriers from automatic routing without altering their other contents or components.
scope: Canonical C11 source for Minecraft Java 26.2 Fabric, historically versioned 0.3.6-external-quick-move-priority-fix-canary, reconstructed from frozen legacy source checkpoint 64d63d9bcca268297601af5c9a7537e8d8946812.

Passive ground pickup and external-container QUICK_MOVE priority through component-identical occupied main hand, qualifying carried containers, occupied hotbar, occupied offhand, compatible ordinary-storage partials, empty hotbar, and empty ordinary storage.
Player-origin QUICK_MOVE routing to a component-identical occupied offhand and qualifying carried containers before returning exact remainder ownership to the active menu's normal algorithm.
Creative and Survival inventory snapshot alignment, source cleanup and menu callbacks, exact remainder accounting, stable carrier order, and persistent per-carrier auto-routing lock state.

exclusions: Equipment, Trinkets, trash, and foreign menu slots are never routing destinations.
Locked, empty, unrelated, full, or component-distinct carried containers cannot claim a new item type.
Inventory Extended and Offhand Shift-Click QoL remain separate optional owners; their code and artifacts are not bundled or migrated here.

Earlier C7-C9 failed or superseded canary binaries and legacy status READMEs, BUILD_PROVENANCE, accumulated test matrices, global status records, manager state, snapshots, and notes remain only in the frozen historical repository.
This migration does not deploy to Minecraft, alter either Test Slot or the accepted physical baseline, launch Minecraft, or access the protected gameplay instance.
